title: Label the problem
prompt: The data team wants a list of the invalid transactions, each with the reason it failed. Write `solve(transactions)` so it returns `transaction_id` and `problem` for every transaction that breaks a rule.
rules: Check the rules in this order and use the first one broken: `no account` (missing `account_id`), `bad amount` (missing or not more than 0), `bad currency` (missing or not `USD`, `EUR` or `GBP`), `wrong direction`.
`purchase`, `atm_withdrawal` and `fee` must have `direction` `debit`; every other type must be `credit`. A missing direction is wrong.
Return only the invalid transactions, with only `transaction_id` and `problem`.
hints: Chain the rules with `F.when(...).when(...)` in the order given; leave out `otherwise` so valid rows get NULL.
Work out the expected direction with its own `F.when(...).otherwise(...)`, then compare it with `direction`. Remember a missing direction.
Select `transaction_id` and the label, then filter for rows where the label `isNotNull()`.
